title: Carver / qoppac: simple breakout trading rule (range-position forecast, pysystemtrade)
why: Continuous rule, not a channel entry: for each lookback N in 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320 business days, roll_max and roll_min over N closes; roll_mean = (roll_max + roll_min)/2; raw = 40 x (price - roll_mean) / (roll_max - roll_min), so about -20 to +20; smooth with an EWMA of span max(int(N/4),1) (the post's example: 63 on 250); the average of the six forecasts is the signal (the post's own cap is +/-20, its scalars are 0.71-0.84 per variant, pooled). Position = forecast / 10 (average absolute forecast about 10), one unit per instrument, daily rebalance, sign-to-size. Sits outside the engine's rule set (no continuous forecast), so the builder writes it as a daily script on closes up to yesterday, with half-round-trip cost per unit of change and 0.5 bp swap per day. Markets: XAUUSD, XAGUSD, WTIUSD, SPXUSD, USDJPY, EURUSD, AUDCAD (daily closes from marketdata). Note: the post has no Sharpe or cost figures; the 10-day variant is costly (turnover about 89 trades a year), so test 20-320 first. Suits Funded (low turnover, daily) more than Hydra. Not the rejected 'channel breakout' entry rule: that was a binary Donchian entry; this is a smoothed range-position forecast.

title: Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling & Schrimpf (2017), Currency Value, Review of Financial Studies 30(2), read in full (54 pages)
why: Rule (Sec. 3.4.1, eq. 7-8): signal = 5-year change in the log real exchange rate, q = p - p* - s (s = USD per unit of foreign currency, CPI prices, base 1970Q1; a higher q is a stronger dollar). Each quarter rank the currencies on the signal and go long the cheap ones (low 5-year change in q, i.e. weak RER vs USD) and short the rich ones, equal-weight rank portfolio or linear weights c_t(x_j - mean), dollar-neutral, rebalanced at quarter end, excess return = spot change plus interest differential. Paper result (22 currencies, 1976Q1-2014Q1, gross, no costs stated): raw 5-year RER rank portfolio SR 0.50 (Table 4), quarterly turnover about 18% (footnote 17). Only the raw PPP version is testable: the fundamentals-adjusted version (SR 0.8-0.9, Table 5) needs GDP per capita, export quality (IMF) and net foreign assets, not free to us. Expected weakness, stated up front: the paper's spread is driven by emerging currencies (Turkey, Mexico, Indonesia, Hungary), so on our 7 USD majors (EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, USDCAD, USDCHF, NZDUSD) with about 0.2 of the paper's dispersion the edge may vanish. Quarterly trades, so the cost is trivial. Suits Funded only (a slow, low-turnover diversifier and keep-the-account leg); not Hydra (a quarter-long hold cannot reach 5x in a month). Needs data item data_fred_cpi_g10 first.

title: Moreira & Muir (2016/2017), Volatility-Managed Portfolios, NBER WP 22208 (read in full, 57 pages incl. appendix)
why: Rule (main text, f^sigma_{t+1} = (c / RV_t^2) * f_{t+1}): RV_t = realized variance of daily returns over the previous month (22 daily returns in a daily version); the managed exposure is c / RV^2 times the buy-and-hold exposure, rebalanced from closes up to yesterday. c sets the managed series' full-sample std equal to buy-and-hold's; for us fit c on data to 2017 only, then freeze it. Cap the scale (test 1x, 2x) since the paper's leverage-cap table in the appendix shows the gain depends on capping. Paper results (monthly, 1926-2015): managed market factor raises Sharpe; OECD 20-country check gives a mean Sharpe change of 0.15 and a positive change in 80% of countries (Fig 8). Markets: SPXUSD and XAUUSD on daily closes (equity-factor paper; the gold leg is an extension and must be labelled so), USDJPY and EURUSD as a check. Costs: half round-trip per unit of position change plus 0.5 bp swap per day. Needs a daily script (the spec engine has no vol-scaling rule). Suits Funded (drawdown control, keep-the-account leg); weak for Hydra (it trims size and does not give the 5x path).

title: Meta-labeling sizing of the AurumBreakout leg (Lopez de Prado, AFML ch. 3.6; Joubert, Meta-Labeling: Calibration and Position Sizing, J. Financial Data Science)
why: Gap: the book's 19 losing months since 2018 (gaps.json), breakout is the largest weight (0.25). Primary model = the existing breakout leg unchanged (side and exits fixed; take every trade the leg takes on USDJPY, EURJPY, GBPUSD, XAUUSD, EURUSD with the leg's own parameters from research/breakout_markets.py). Meta label = 1 if the trade's net R > 0. Features, all known at entry: ATR(14)/ATR(100) ratio, 20-day realised vol percentile, distance of entry from 20-day mean in ATRs, entry hour, weekday, prior 5-trade hit rate of the same market, prior-day range/ATR, month-end flag. Model: sklearn logistic regression (L2) and a shallow LightGBM (depth 2, 100 trees) as a check; expanding walk-forward, retrain each January on all earlier trades with a 10-day purge, first test year 2012, so both halves (2012-17, 2018+) are out of sample. Use: size = 0.5 + 0.5 x calibrated p, or skip when p < 0.40, never above 1x, so it can only trim the leg. Published basis: meta-labeling is the López de Prado method for sizing a fixed-side primary model (only the Hudson and Thames explainer was readable in full; the book chapter and Joubert paper are paywalled, so belief rests on the method plus the 5-market pooling). Differs from the rejected meta_label_hydra (2026-10-22: 2,896 tester trades of Hydra, no skill, tiny sample): different leg, about 15 years of trades pooled across 5 markets, past-only features, walk-forward from 2012. Closest rejected family in candidates.md is 'daily ML'; this is trade-level sizing, not a daily direction forecast. Pass test: the sized leg's Sharpe >= the plain leg in both halves, lower worst month, corr to book unchanged. If no lift over a random-keep at the same rate (3 seeds), reject, as with Hydra. Suits Funded (drawdown and losing-month control); Hydra no.

title: Harvey, Mazzoleni & Melone (2025), The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing (SSRN 5122748), pp1-22 read, pages 23-76 not read (robustness, appendix)
why: Gap: US indices (4% of risk), cross-asset flow style, daily horizon, and the book losing months. Rule: simulate a 60/40 portfolio of S&P 500 and 10y Treasury (eq. in Sec 1.2): w(t+1)=w(1+Rsp)/(w(1+Rsp)+(1-w)(1+R10y)), target 60%. Threshold signal_t = mean over delta=0,0.1,...,2.5% of (w_t - 0.60), where w resets to 0.60 whenever |w-0.60|>delta. Calendar signal_t = w_t - 0.60 with reset on the last business day of each month, used only in the last 5 trading days of the month. Both predict next-day S&P minus 10y return NEGATIVELY (t about 4; Table 1 coefficients -0.42 Threshold, -0.30 Calendar*week4; 1 sd = about 17-20 bp next day; reverts within 2 weeks; effect significant only from early 2000s). Paper: front-running S&P/10y futures long-short on these signals Sharpe > 1, 1997-2023 (gross; page of the Sharpe table not located in the pages read). Our test: equity side only, since FTMO has no bond CFD: short US500.cash next day when signal > 0 and long when < 0 (threshold signal anytime; calendar signal in last-5-day window), one position per day, cost = US500 spread + FTMO swap from docs/ftmo_specs.json. Bond leg input: R10y approx = -8 x change in DGS10 (percent/100) + DGS10/252 from FRED DGS10 daily (free CSV, see data_fred_dgs10); S&P daily close-to-close from marketdata. Same parameters on US100.cash and GER40 if held as the 3-market belief check (paper: signal extends to international equity). Expected weakness: published sample ends 2023-03, flow edge may have decayed; equity-only leg loses the bond half of the spread. Different from rejected noise leg/overnight and the leveraged-ETF rebalancing idea (single stocks): this is pension month-end flow on the index. Suits Funded (daily, low risk); Hydra small add-on.

title: Dao, McGroarty, Urquhart (2016), A calendar effect: weekend overreaction (and subsequent reversal) in spot FX rates, JMulFin 37-38 (read in full, 22 pages)
why: Gap: EURUSD (no leg), weeks/days horizon, mean-reversion style, FX majors outside the quartet/breakout legs; trades about 10% of weeks so it should be near-zero corr with the book. Rule (Sec 3.1-3.2, Tables 4-9): weekend gap = ln(Monday open / Friday close) (paper: Monday open = Sunday 22:00 GMT, Friday close = 22:00 GMT; on FTMO data use first M1 bar of the week and last bar of Friday). Large gap = top or bottom 5% quantile of past weekend gaps of the same pair (5-year window 2002-06, then recursive or rolling; we use a rolling 260-week window, past weeks only). Trade at the Monday open OPPOSITE to the gap (short after top-5% gap, long after bottom-5%), exit at Friday close (one-week horizon, the most significant; 1-day and 3-day horizons are weaker). One position per pair per week. Paper results, 7 majors 2007-2014 out of sample, round-trip cost 0.08% and interest included: abnormal weekly alpha NZDUSD 0.19-0.20% (t>3), GBPUSD 0.07%, CHFUSD 0.05%, EURUSD 0.04% (n.s.), JPY/CAD/AUD about 0; majors group alpha 0.05-0.06% a week (t about 2.5); max drawdown 2-24%; reversal larger after upward gaps (top 5%: EURUSD -0.45% next week, NZDUSD -1.16%) than after downward gaps (bottom 5%: +0.43% panel mean). Panel-mean one-week reversal in Table 4 is -0.33%/+0.43% (top/bottom 5%). Our test: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD, AUDCAD with identical parameters (belief by 3+ markets; do not pick pairs by result), real FTMO spread (about 1-2 bp, far below the paper cost 8 bp, so costs are friendlier) plus FTMO swap for the 5 nights from docs/ftmo_specs.json; report halves (2010-17 / 2018 on), 1.5x cost, per-pair Sharpe, trade count, corr to the book and book gain. Expected weakness: sample ends 2014, few trades per pair (about 30 a decade at 5% each side), the effect may have decayed like other published FX calendar effects (Breedon-Ranaldo failed halves); a Sharpe 0.2-0.5 basket is the aim. Differs from the dropped Monday gap fill statistics (intraday vendor fill rates, no net test) and from the rejected round-number and daily reversal grids (this is a weekly hold after a rare gap). Suits Funded; Hydra no.

title: Caporale & Plastun (2019), Price Overreactions in the Forex and Trading Strategies, Brunel WP 19-09 (pp1-14 read; remainder is appendix tables)
why: Gap: EURUSD (no leg), days horizon, Asian-session timing, mean-reversion after shocks; trades ~6-8 days a year per pair so near-zero corr with book expected. Rule (Sec 3-4): daily return R=Close/Open-1 (open to close of the day, gaps excluded). Positive overreaction when R > mean_n + k*sd_n, negative when R < mean_n - k*sd_n, k=2; paper does not state n, so use n=20 days of past daily returns fixed, no sweep. Strategy 2 (the one to test first): at the start of the day AFTER an overreaction day open a position opposite to the overreaction and close it at the start of the European session (paper: 07:00-09:00 broker time; use 08:00 fixed, no tuning); paper finds the contrarian move only in Asia, 00:00-09:00. Paper results 2008-2018, hourly MetaQuotes data, NO costs, t-tests vs random: positive overreaction fade EURUSD 0.77%/yr (67 trades, 66% wins), USDJPY 1.37%, AUDUSD 2.29%, EURJPY 2.11%, USDCAD none; negative overreaction fade EURUSD 0.5% (not sig), USDJPY 2.0%, AUDUSD 1.7%, EURJPY 1.8% (n.s.), USDCAD 0.6% n.s. title: Trend strength with cubic reversion (Safari & Schmidhuber 2025, arXiv 2501.16772): fade strong multi-day trends, follow weak ones, daily on gold/EURUSD/USDJPY/US500/US100/AUDCAD
why: Gap: days horizon, mean-reversion style on the extremes (steer: thin horizon days). Paper read pp1-16 of 38 (abstract, Sec 2 daily method, Table 3, Sec 3 intraday start; monthly/yearly sections and the appendix not read). Definition: normalised daily log return R = (r - mu)/sigma (mu, sigma past-only here); trend strength phi_T(t) = sum_n w_T(n) R(t-n) with w_T(n) = M_T * n * exp(-2n/T), M_T set so sum w^2 = 1 (phi is a t-statistic), clipped to +/-2.5, T = 2^k days for k=1..10. Next-day model R(t+1) = a + b*phi + c*phi^3 with, pooled over 24 futures (S&P, DAX, Nikkei, EUR/USD, JPY/USD, GBP/USD, gold, crude and others) and 10 horizons, 1990-2020: b = 1.29% (t 3.0), c = -0.62% (t 2.7); bootstrapped errors 3-4x the naive ones; b is decaying toward 0 over the decades, c stable. So: weak trend persists, expected return changes sign at |phi| = sqrt(b/|c|) = 1.44 and is negative beyond it (fade the strong trend); the mean of the 10 phi is a stronger single predictor (out-of-sample R2 4.9 bp aggregated vs 1.3 bp single). Our rule, fixed: phi_bar = mean of the 10 phi_T (T = 2..1024 days, past-only at the close); position next day proportional to b*phi_bar + c*phi_bar^3 with b = 1.29, c = -0.62 (published values, not refitted), clipped at +/-1 unit, scaled by 60-day vol for equal risk; test also the extreme-only part (position -sign(phi_bar) when |phi_bar| > 1.44, else flat). title: Keloharju, Linnainmaa, Nyberg (2016, JF) Return Seasonalities: same-calendar-month commodity long-short
why: Read pp.1-5, 20-32 (Sec 5.4.3, Table 8 Panel C). Rule from the paper: each month t, for every commodity with >=5 years of history, average its return in calendar month t over all prior years; go long the top group and short the bottom group for that month, hold to month end. Paper: 24 commodity futures 1970-2011, long-short 0.93%/month (t 1.93); the placebo (rank by average of the OTHER 11 calendar months) earns -0.22% (t -0.58), difference t 1.97. Country indexes: 0.48%/mo (t 2.20). Seasonality strategies correlate negligibly across asset classes (Sec 5.5). Our test: daily continuous futures already in marketdata/commod (CL,BZ,NG,HG,GC,SI,PL,PA,ZC,ZS,ZW,CT,CC,KC,SB,OJ; 2005-2026), first signal 2010 (5y history), top 3 / bottom 3 of the ~16, equal risk (inverse 60d vol), month-end rebalance, research only to 2025-10-10; halves 2010-2017 / 2018+. Run the placebo (other-month rank) alongside; it must fail. Trade on FTMO CFDs (XAUUSD, XAGUSD, XPTUSD, XPDUSD, XCUUSD, USOIL/UKOIL, NATGAS, CORN, WHEAT, SOYBEAN, COTTON, COFFEE, SUGAR, COCOA; OJ has no FTMO symbol so drop it for the gate run); cost = FTMO spread + swap for a month hold. Gap: commodities/non-FX market with no leg, monthly horizon (weeks+), market-neutral so low corr to the book expected (<0.1; only gold overlaps). Suits Funded (monthly, small turnover); too slow for Hydra. Not carry/VRP/TSMOM/COT/FX calendar. Weak alone is fine: a Sharpe 0.2-0.5 unrelated leg is welcome. Not in rejected index or memory (searched same-calendar-month, seasonality commodity).
result: gate halves: 1x SR -0.24/0.30 (gross 0.22/0.69), 1.5x -0.16; costs+financing eat the edge; see research/commod_same_month.py

title: Liu, Tsyvinski, Wu (2019/2022 JF) Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency: weekly cross-sectional 1-4 week momentum, market-neutral
why: Read pp.1-4 plus the companion w24877 (Liu-Tsyvinski) tables 14-17 pp.20-24 in full. Paper rule: each week sort coins by past 1-, 2-, 3- or 4-week return, long top quintile, short bottom quintile, hold the next week (paper: 2.7/3.3/4.1/2.5%/week long-short on 1,600 coins 2014-18, t>2). Suits Funded only (weekend gaps, high vol: size small).

title: HAR-RV volatility forecast to size the breakout and noise legs (Corsi 2009)
why: Gap: the book losing months (19 of 94; 2021-11 -8.0%, 2023-05 -6.2%) and sizing. Model: Corsi HAR-RV, RV_next = b0 + bd*RV_d + bw*RV_w(5d mean) + bm*RV_m(22d mean), OLS on log daily realised vol from M5 returns of each leg own market (breakout: USDJPY; noise: US100/US500), expanding-window refit monthly, past-only. Use: leg size multiplier = clip(median_vol_250d / forecast_vol, 0.5, 1.5) instead of the current trailing vol scaling, applied to the leg own daily P&L from the leg trade list (research only to 2025-10-10). Closest rejected: ml_metalabel_breakout_size (AUC 0.51-0.53, a classifier on trades) and meta_label_hydra; differs: target is volatility (highly predictable, R2 0.4-0.6 in the HAR literature), not trade sign, so there is no dependence on a weak label. Same parameters on both legs and a third check on cross (belief: 2 of 3 legs improve). Gate: leg Sharpe halves each >= 0.2 after the sizing change, book 2018+ from 3.01 up >= 0.03, report change in the 19 losing months and worst month. Control: random multiplier with the same distribution. Counts in DSR N. Suits Funded (cap risk, losing months); Hydra no.

title: Two-state Gaussian HMM on book daily return and vol: cut book risk in the bad regime
why: Gap: the book losing months, broad ones (2021-11, 2023-05) not owned by one leg. Honest expectation: a vol-clustering effect already in the risk layer; accept only if book Sharpe 2018+ rises >= 0.03 with halves each not lower and a random-halving control at the same fraction of days does worse. title: Kaufman efficiency-ratio start filter on the AUDCAD grid leg
why: Leg: grid (mean reversion, days, S2018 0.75; book without it 3.18 vs 3.01 so it is the weakest-adding leg and loses in trends: book losing months 2021-11, 2023-05). Rule, no fitting: ER = |close[t]-close[t-N]| / sum|daily change| over N=10 days (Kaufman 1995/2013 definition), computed on AUDCAD daily closes known before the day. Skip opening a new grid cycle when ER > 0.5 (strong trend); N=10 and 0.5 fixed in advance, plus the one robustness pair N=20 / 0.4, both reported and counted in the DSR N. Same filter applied to the other mean-reversion legs only if the grid improves. title: Heston, Korajczyk, Sadka (2010) intraday return periodicity at daily lags, on EURUSD, XAUUSD, USDJPY, US500, US100
why: Gap: EURUSD has no leg, intraday seasonal style. Paper (JF 65): return in a given half-hour slot predicts the return in the same slot on later days at lags of 1..40 trading days (lags that are multiples of 1 day, positive, strongest at lag 1 and multiples of 5). Stock-level in the paper, so belief rests on the rule being run with identical parameters on 5 markets, as steer.md says the builder measures costs. Rule: for each hour h (server time, rollover 23-01 excluded), signal = mean of the h-hour returns over the last 20 trading days (lags 1-20, past only); go long (short) the next day h-hour if signal is in the top (bottom) tercile of its trailing 250-day distribution; hold 1 hour; enter at hour open, M1 data from histdata, FTMO spreads. Same parameters on all 5 markets; report per-market halves. Note the quartet leg is a seasonal-session leg (corr must be checked <= 0.30; if signal repeats quartet hours it fails corr). Number of trials: 24 hours x 5 markets counts in the DSR N. Suits Funded; Hydra only if it passes.

title: Erb & Harvey (2013) golden dilemma: gold vs rate shocks, DGS10 5-day change as weekly signal on XAUUSD, USDJPY, US100
why: Gap: gold/USDJPY weeks, off-intraday, may earn when the gold trend reverses (hold-leg losing months 2021-11, 2023-05). Rule (pre-registered, same params on 3 markets): dy = DGS10 change over last 5 trading days (FRED, free, in marketdata/fred/DGS10.csv), z = dy / 60d sd of dy. Closest rejected: policy_gap_eurusd_weeks (level gap) and trend rules; counts as 1 DSR trial per market. Low expected corr with hold (gold trend) as the signal is a rate shock; check corr. title: Cieslak, Morse & Vissing-Jorgensen, Stock Returns over the FOMC Cycle (J. Finance 2019; Oct 2015 draft read pp.1-12 of 70)
why: GAP: US indices (4% of risk), days horizon, calendar style not covered by the legs. Paper (Sec 2f, Table 3 Strategy B): FOMC cycle time starts the day before each scheduled announcement day (day -1 = trading day before; day 0 = announcement day). Even weeks: week 0 = days -1..3, week 2 = days 9..13, week 4 = days 19..23, week 6 = days 29..33 (trading days). Hold the index long only in even weeks, flat in odd weeks (Sharpe 0.8 vs 0.4 buy-and-hold, 1994-2013; even-week 5-day excess return 0.57/0.30/0.42/0.61%, odd weeks about -0.1 to -0.17%). Rule to test with fixed paper parameters on US500, US100 (long even weeks only; flat in odd weeks, no shorting, since Strategy D has worse Sharpe), belief check on GER40 (next-day, time-zone lag) and XAUUSD with the same rule; run also the weeks-2,4,6-only variant to avoid overlap with the rejected pre-FOMC drift (Lucca-Moench). Risk: effect was documented 1994-2013, may have faded after (check the 2018-on half; honest halves gate). The 2019 JF version may differ from the draft in detail. Suits Funded (low-vol index overlay) and maybe Hydra only as a filter. Not in rejected list (pre-FOMC drift and totm_us are different windows).

title: Melvin & Prins (BlackRock; J. Financial Markets 2015): equity-hedging flows into the last London 4pm fix of the month, conditioned on the month's equity return
why: Read pp.1-22 (workshop version; appendix is theory). Paper rule: on the last business day of the month, the 15:00-16:00 GMT currency return is predicted by the country's equity return from day 1 to the second-last day, with a NEGATIVE sign (panel coefficient -0.0142, p=0.00, 10 G10 currencies, 2004-2012, relative to cross-section mean; 10% equity gain = 14bp currency fall). Then 72% of that hour's move reverts by noon next day (post-fix reversion coefficient doubles on month-end days, eq.5: 16:00 to next-day 12:00 return on 15:00-16:00 return). Pre-registered rule, same parameters on EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY, AUDUSD, USDCAD (+ XAUUSD not used): signal s = ret(US500 or SPXUSD, month day 1 to second-last close) minus ret(foreign index: GRXEUR for EUR, JPXJPY for JPY; for GBP/AUD/CAD use US500 alone, expressed vs 0). US outperformance -> USD sold in the hour: long EURUSD/GBPUSD/AUDUSD, short USDJPY/USDCAD at 15:00 GMT (check histdata/server-time offset; London 16:00 = fix), exit 16:00. Variant B (the paper's reversion): enter at 16:00 opposite to the run-up, exit next day 12:00 GMT. Variant C: both A and B in one leg. Trade only when |s| exceeds the month's median |s| (one rule, no tuning). About 12 days a year per pair, so the builder must pool pairs and report event counts (expect ~200 per pair 2004-2025; histdata M1 EURUSD from 2004). Gap: EURUSD (no leg), a conditioned flow event rather than the unconditional month-end window. Honest risk: steer.md says fix and cross already trade month-end flows and 1-hour windows may carry little after costs (14bp per 10% equity move vs a 1-1.5bp spread); correlation to fix/cross must be measured and the gate decides. Differs from rejected unconditional month-end specs by the equity-return sign condition. Suits Funded (low frequency, tiny risk) and Hydra only as a minor leg. Counts in DSR N.
result: Fails corr: cross leg +0.53 (limit 0.30); book 2018+ 3.11->3.03. Halves 1.02/0.51, 1.5x 0.61, DSR ok. Duplicates fix/cross month-end flow.

title: Moreira & Muir (JF 2017) volatility-managed sizing applied to the gold hold leg (sizing, not a standalone leg)
why: Read pp.1-12 (definitions, Table 1 setup, MVE section); rest is theory and robustness. Paper rule (eq.1-2): managed return f_sigma(t+1) = c / RV2_t * f(t+1), RV2_t = realized variance of the previous 22 trading days from daily returns, c chosen so the managed series has the same unconditional vol as buy-and-hold (c does not change Sharpe). Paper shows Sharpe up 25% for the market, big alpha for momentum (appraisal 0.88) and the carry factor, and works on 20 OECD indices. Our use differs from the rejected volmanaged_mm (a standalone vol-scaled long leg, halves -0.21/-0.07): here the underlying is an existing positive leg, the HOLD leg (S2018 0.62, trend, weeks+), whose daily pnl is scaled by c/RV2 of the hold leg own pnl over the prior 22 days (past-only, one-day lag), scale clipped to [0.25, 2.0], c set so average scale = 1 over the sample (no free parameter). Same unchanged rule on the other trend-like pnl streams as belief check: grid and breakout leg pnl, and on the XAUUSD, US500, US100 buy-and-hold series (paper claims it on the market factor and momentum). Gate question is the book: does the scaled hold lift book Sharpe from 2018 by >= 0.03 and keep corr low; it also should shrink the hold share of losing months (hold carries 26% of the loss, steer.md). Note: the book risk layer already vol-targets; the builder must test the scaled hold on top of the layer and say if it double counts. Gap: weeks+ horizon, losing months. Suits both (Funded: smaller drawdowns; Hydra: only if it keeps growth). Counts in DSR N, one parameter set, no tuning.
result: book gate: 3.11 -> 2.96 replacing hold; halves 0.42/0.23, costs, corr, DSR pass. Vol-managed hold lowers 2018+ SR 0.53->0.23

title: Ridge-regression sizing of the gold hold leg on trend strength and volatility rank
why: Model: sklearn Ridge (alpha 10, standardised features), walk-forward with an expanding window refit yearly from 2008, past-only. Target: the hold leg next-20-day pnl divided by its trailing 60-day pnl vol. Features (all lagged one day): XAUUSD 21/63/252-day returns divided by 63-day vol, 63-day realized vol percentile rank over 2 years, distance of price from its 200-day mean in vol units, DXY proxy = 63-day return of EURUSD and USDJPY, VIX level from marketdata/fred/VIXCLS (ends 2025-03; use only where present, else drop the feature). Use: size multiplier = clip(1 + k*prediction_z, 0.25, 1.75) with k fixed at 0.5 before the run (no sweep); hold leg only. Success is not the AUC but the book: S2018 and the hold losing-month share. Closest rejected: Deep Momentum Networks (deep, 50 futures, seed-dependent) and ml_regime_grid_audcad (logistic regime classifier, OOF AUC 0.513) and the two meta-label tests (no skill). Differs: linear model on one leg, continuous sizing not a trade filter, target is vol-scaled forward pnl so it can be small and still help. Honest risk: the same AUC-near-0.5 outcome as the regime test; the builder must report the walk-forward IC (needs > 0.05) before gating and stop if lower. Gap: weeks+ horizon, ML on existing legs. Suits Funded and Hydra. Counts in DSR N.

title: Nagel: Evaporating liquidity - VIX-conditioned short-term reversal on US indices
why: Nagel (NBER 17653, read pp1-12): reversal returns = liquidity provision, expected return and conditional Sharpe rise with VIX (3-month avg tracks VIX almost perfectly, no losing 3-month period 1998-2010). title: Gold vs EURUSD residual fade (cross-asset relative value, fills EURUSD gap)
why: Rule, same parameters on 3 pairs: r5 = 5-day log return; residual e = r5(target) - b*r5(anchor) with b a rolling 250-day OLS beta (past only); z = e / rolling 250d sd of e. Fade: short target when z>2, long when z<-2, hold 5 days, exit at z cross 0. Pairs: XAUUSD vs EURUSD (trade gold), EURUSD vs XAUUSD (trade EUR), XAGUSD vs XAUUSD (trade silver). title: Turbulence index (Mahalanobis distance) as a past-only risk scaler on the whole book
why: TI_t=(y_t-mu)' Sigma^-1 (y_t-mu), mu and Sigma from the past 104 weeks (Kritzman-Li 2010 FAJ definition, as restated and read in full in Kamauchi-Yokouchi 2021; Kritzman-Li original paywalled, not read). Rule: weekly TI on 6 daily-return series (XAUUSD, US500, US100, EURUSD, USDJPY, AUDCAD) summed to weekly, window 104w; weight on the book = 1.0 minus 0.4 x percentile rank of the 13-week average TI within the last 104 weeks (range 0.6-1.0, authors TI portfolio form 80%-40%*rank), applied to all legs of the book the next week; past-only, no fit. Fills gap: losing months (2021-11 -8.5%, 2023-05 -6.2%, 2024-05 -4.2%) as a book overlay, not a new leg. Gate is book Sharpe/maxDD/losing-month count from 2018 vs unscaled book, halves each >=0.2 unchanged. title: Driesprong, Jacobsen, Maat 2008: a fall in oil predicts a higher stock index next month (hold the index only after a negative oil month)
why: Read pp1-24 in full (ERIM working paper of the JFE 2008 article, doi 10.1016/j.jfineco.2007.07.008, J. Financial Economics 89(2) 307-327). Finding: the monthly oil change predicts the next month's stock return with a NEGATIVE sign (a rise in oil is followed by lower stock returns), significant in most developed markets, read as investor underreaction, strongest in the first month. Rule: at each month-end, if the WTI front-month return of the month just ended is below 0, go long the index for the next calendar month; if above 0, stay flat (long-only variant; the short side only if the gates allow). Same parameters, no fitting, on US500, GER40 and JPN225 (UK100 as a belief check), index CFDs at FTMO; monthly turnover, so the cost is one spread per switch plus overnight swap (US500 long about 2.5 bp/night). Data: marketdata/commod CL daily (cut at 2025-10-10; month return of the continuous series with roll days zeroed), histdata SPXUSD, GRXEUR, JPXJPY. Gap filled: indices on weeks+ (indices hold 4% of risk, 8 of 10 legs are intraday), an oil-to-equity cross-asset signal; not carry/VRP/TSMOM/COT/calendar (the signal is another market's return). Expected corr <= 0.30: the book has no monthly index exposure (noise is intraday) and hold (gold trend) should be near 0. Suits Funded (monthly, low frequency); Hydra only if both halves pass.
evidence: The paper's own result is in-sample and published 2008; post-publication confirmation is weak (later work finds the oil-stock link unstable, and Japan is insignificant in the paper itself). Honest low prior: if either half (before/after 2018) is below 0.2 it is rejected. Not tested in this repo (memory search found no hit).
result: Rebuilt from the paper's regression rule (eq.1, fitted to 2017, long if fitted return > 0) with ftmo_specs costs on US500/GER40/JP225: oil slope t ~0 in 2011-17 and 2018+, so the rule is always long; halves 0.27/0.18, 1.5x -0.01, corr -0.09, book 2018+ 3.11->3.08 (needs +0.03), dsr 1.0. Finder's oil<0 variant (not the paper's rule): halves 0.18/0.34, 1.5x 0.12, book 3.10. Rejected

title: Chen, Rogoff, Rossi 2010: commodity currencies (AUD, CAD, NZD) lead commodity prices, trade metals and oil on the monthly sign of the currency basket
why: Read pp1-30 of 49 (NBER w13901, Quarterly Journal of Economics 125(3) 1145-1194, 'Can Exchange Rates Forecast Commodity Prices?'). Finding: exchange rates of commodity exporters (Australia, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa, Chile) help forecast world commodity prices, the currency leading and the sign positive (a stronger commodity currency forecasts higher commodity prices), best in forecast combination and for index, metals and oil. Rule: at each month-end compute the equal-weight month return of AUDUSD, NZDUSD and inverted USDCAD; if positive go long, if negative go short for the next month on XCUUSD (or XAGUSD) and USOIL, same parameters on all, no fit. Check swaps first (copper/platinum/palladium long swaps are large, the short side is cheaper) in docs/ftmo_specs.json. Data: fred/DEXUSAL, DEXUSNZ, DEXCAUS (daily, 1971 on) or histdata M1; commodities from marketdata/commod CL, HG, SI (cut at 2025-10-10, roll days zeroed). Gap filled: off-gold, off-intraday (weeks), a different asset and information set that may earn when the gold trend reverses. Expected corr <= 0.30: the book trades FX majors intraday and gold; a monthly commodity position shares no bet with it. Not carry/TSMOM (the signal is another market's return). Suits Funded; Hydra only if halves pass.
evidence: The paper's evidence is quarterly to 2008 with time-varying parameters and forecast combination; it gives no tradable monthly result and no post-publication test. Low belief, honest label. Pass criterion is the repo gate (both halves >= 0.2 after costs and swap, profitable at 1.5x costs).

title: Sorensen 2002: harvest-pressure seasonal in grains, short corn, soybean and wheat from 1 June to 30 September
why: Paper: Carsten Sorensen, 'Modeling Seasonality in Agricultural Commodity Futures', J. Futures Markets 22(5), 2002 (CBS working paper 2002_004). Agricultural futures carry a seasonal that follows the crop cycle: prices are higher before harvest and lower after, because the harvest supply shock and inventories push them down in summer to early autumn. Rule: short corn, soybean and wheat (CORN.c, SOYBEAN.c, WHEAT.c; COTTON.c as a belief market) from the close of 31 May to the close of 30 September each year, same dates on all, flat otherwise, no fitting. The short swap at FTMO is positive on grains (long grains pay large swaps), so carry works for it. Data: marketdata/commod daily ZC, ZS, ZW, CT up to 2025-10-10. WARNING: the series is unadjusted continuous front-month with roll jumps, so the builder must roll-adjust (back-adjust or zero the roll days); my own roll-zeroed screen on pre-cutoff data gave ZC about +6.5% and ZS about +2.8% over the window in the short direction and wheat about 0 (a screen, not a result). Gap filled: off-gold, off-FX, weeks horizon, agriculture (no agricultural leg in the book). Expected corr <= 0.30: nothing in the book is agricultural and a 4-month seasonal short has no link to intraday FX/gold. Funded only for now (low frequency, month-scale drawdowns); Hydra only if halves pass and the stress months are acceptable.

title: Fernandez-Perez, Frijns, Fuertes, Miffre 2018: long the most negatively skewed commodities, short the most positively skewed, monthly
why: Paper read in full (44 pp; J. Banking & Finance 86:143-158, 2018). Rule (their eq. 1, section 4): at each month-end compute the Pearson skewness of the past 12 months of daily front-contract returns for each commodity, rank the cross-section, long the lowest quintile (most negative skew), short the highest quintile (most positive skew), equal weight, hold one month (R=12, H=1). Their result: 8.01% a year, t=3.83, Sharpe 0.78, alpha 6.58% (t=3.58) after the four commodity factors; the short side (Q5, -10.9% a year) does most of the work; robust to skew from filtered returns, liquidity filter and 2x costs (break-even cost 0.93% a trade); holding periods 3-12 months leave the finding unchanged (their footnote 7). Mechanism: cumulative prospect theory plus selective hedging, so positively skewed (lottery-like) commodities are overpriced. Our version on the FTMO-tradable set with daily data in marketdata/commod: CC (COCOA.c), KC (COFFEE.c), ZC (CORN.c), CT (COTTON.c), ZS (SOYBEAN.c), SB (SUGAR.c), ZW (WHEAT.c), CL (USOIL), BZ (UKOIL), NG (NATGAS.cash), HG (XCUUSD), GC (XAUUSD), SI (XAGUSD), PL (XPTUSD), PA (XPDUSD) = 15 markets, quintile = top 3 and bottom 3, same parameters on all, no fitting; also test the 20%/40% cut and the n=2 version only as belief checks. Gap filled: a style with no leg (skewness, not carry, not trend, not VRP: the paper shows near-zero correlation to the term-structure, momentum and hedging-pressure factors, adj R2 5.7%), the weeks horizon (monthly hold) and off-gold/FX/index markets (soft commodities and energy). Expected corr <= 0.30: a monthly cross-sectional commodity long/short has no clock, no FX-dollar exposure and the book is 8 of 10 intraday; grains and softs are not held by any leg. Not TSMOM (cross-sectional, market-neutral, sign set by skew). Costs the builder must charge: FTMO swap on each leg from docs/ftmo_specs.json (grains pay on the short side, XPT/XPD swaps are negative on both sides), spread each monthly turn. Suits Funded first (low vol, monthly, no overnight gap risk beyond the hold) and Hydra as a small-weight leg. Data cut at 2025-10-10. Roll artefacts: marketdata/commod are unadjusted continuous front series; skewness is very sensitive to a roll jump or the CL negative-price day (2020-04), so zero the roll days (as the Sorensen build did) and drop 2020-04-20/21 for CL before computing skew; report with and without that fix. Different from the Sorensen grain seasonal (rejected at book, calendar) and from futures_tsmom/COT (rejected): signal is the third moment of daily returns, rebalanced on rank.
evidence: The paper's own sample is 1987-2014 (27 commodities), so only the part before 2014 is in-sample publication-era; its Sharpe 0.78 is on the full 27 set. Post-publication: Quantpedia strategy 281 (Vojtko and Padysak, https://quantpedia.com/strategies/skewness-effect-in-commodities) reports an independent replication of about 8.5% a year from 1991 to 2019 (drawdown quoted inconsistently, 16% or 54%), so only partly independent and not past 2019. No source tests 2019-2025 or the 15-market CFD subset; with 15 names the long/short legs are 3 markets each, so expect a lower Sharpe (guess 0.3-0.5) and a noisy halves test. Honest medium-low prior; the useful property is the near-zero correlation to the intraday book.
result: gates FAIL at halves -1.31/-2.78; gross no-swap Sharpe -0.08 (halves -0.23/+0.15), FTMO swap drag ~-49%/yr; costs -1.92, book 3.11->2.48. research/commod_skew_ls.py

title: Thompson-sampling bandit over leg risk multipliers (0.5/1/1.5), monthly walk-forward

Closest rejected: ml_hold_ridge_sizing (one leg, features, SR 0.14 to 2017) and EIIE/PPO sizing (deep, daily); this one is a 3-arm bandit, monthly, no features, same rule on all 10 legs. title: Hierarchical Risk Parity weights across the book legs (Lopez de Prado 2016, JPM 42(4))
why: Sizing of existing legs, not a new leg. Paper (read in full, 31 pp, mirror smallake.kr SSRN-id2708678.pdf): stage 1 single-linkage tree on d=sqrt((1-rho)/2); stage 2 quasi-diagonal sort; stage 3 recursive bisection, weight split by inverse cluster variance (cluster var from IVP weights). Test: every month from 2018 estimate daily pnl covariance of the 10 book legs (quartet, grid, hold, fix, cross, fall, morning, after, breakout, noise) on the trailing 260 days (past only), set leg risk by HRP, rebalance every 22 days, compare with the current equal risk: book Sharpe from 2018, DSR, losing months (21 of 94) and max DD. Differs from rejected DRL allocators: no RL, no return forecast, only past covariance. Honest caveat: leg corr is already <=0.18, so HRP will be near inverse-variance; gain expected small, a cheap test. Counts in DSR N. Suits Funded and Hydra (weights only).

title: Trend-day versus range-day classifier (Dalton, Mind over Markets) gating breakout, noise and grid
why: Own legs: breakout, noise, grid (losing months list in docs/gaps.json: 21 of 94; 2021-11, 2023-05, 2024-05 broad). Label per day and market: trend day if |close-open| >= 0.6 of the day range, else range day. Features known before each leg's entry only: Asian-session range / 20d median, overnight gap / ATR, prior-day type, prior-day range ratio, hour of week, VIX level (marketdata/vixidx). Model: shallow LightGBM or logistic, expanding window refit every 3 months from 2010, train on data before the test year. Use: scale breakout and noise risk by P(trend) (0 below 0.4, full above 0.55), grid by P(range); no new trades, so no new entries to fit. Closest rejected: ml_regime_grid_audcad and ml_regime_hmm_book (HMM / regime on daily returns, unsupervised); this one is supervised on an intraday-day-type label with intraday features and gates three legs on the same label. Report book Sharpe from 2018, losing months, and the DSR with N counting each gated leg. Suits Funded and Hydra (sizing only).

why: Pre-registered single change to the existing grid leg (AUDCAD, days): run the grid only on days when the Lo-MacKinlay VR(5) of AUDCAD daily log returns over the past 120 days is below 1 (mean-reverting, past-only, no fitting; one threshold 1.0, one window 120, one q 5). title: Statistical jump model (JM) 0/1 regime filter: long US500 / US100 only in the bull regime
why: Shu, Yu, Mulvey (2024) Downside risk reduction using regime-switching signals. Rule: 2-state statistical jump model (k-means with a jump penalty lambda per regime switch) fitted on features of the index excess return series: EWM downside deviation halflife 10d, EWM Sortino halflife 20d and 60d; lambda fixed at 50 (paper's typical value, 0.8 shifts a year; do NOT tune lambda on our data); params refit every 6 months on a 3000-day window, online state from DP over the last 3000 days; bull regime = state with higher cumulative training return. Signal at close of day t is traded from day t+2 (1-day delay). Long the index in bull, flat in bear. Markets: US500, US100 (CFD), same parameters on GRXEUR and JPXJPY as a check; use daily index history before 2010 (commod/ futures or histdata) only as the 3000-day burn-in. Long-only index, weeks+ horizon, about 0.8 trades a year, so gate on N and on halves. Gap filled: thin weeks+ horizon, US indices (4% of risk); a market-regime long should have low correlation to the intraday legs and to the gold hold (aim corr <= 0.30; also check against noise leg). Closest rejected: HMM regime trend filter on FX/gold (decisions 2026-10-23), different here because the JM penalty makes regimes persistent (HMM 2-8 shifts a year against JM under 1) and it is a long-only index exposure, not a trend filter on FX. Suits Funded (low drawdown) and not Hydra. Pre-registered: one parameter set, counts in the DSR N.

Not a post-2018-only table; the filter is judged by our own 2018+ half.

title: Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (2021 JFE): market intraday momentum, return to 30 min before close predicts the last 30 min, on US500, US100 (+ DAX, Nikkei same rule)
why: Gap: US indices (4% of book risk) and a thin 30-minute close window; expected corr to the book ~0 (noise leg holds intraday on open-to-close breakouts, this trades only the last 30 min; check corr with noise first). Read in full: Sec 2-3, Tables 2,4,5,6,7. Rule (eq 12): r_ROD = price at close-30min / previous close - 1 (r_ROD includes the overnight gap). If r_ROD>0 go long at close-30min, else short; exit at the cash close. Same parameters on US500, US100, GRXEUR (DAX), JPXJPY (Nikkei) cash-session times; US cash close 16:00 NY (FTMO server ~22:00-23:00 depending on DST, so enter ~21:30 and exit by 21:55 server in US DST mismatch weeks; build session times from the cash calendar, keep out of the 23:00-01:00 rollover per lesson 9). Variant allowed (paper eq 5 and Table 6): only trade when r_ROD and r_ONFH (first 30 min incl. overnight) share the sign (SR 1.60 vs 1.73 gross, fewer trades). Paper mechanism: gamma hedging of option makers and leveraged ETFs; effect concentrated when net gamma negative (Table 7: beta 6.63 t 4.78 vs 0.82 t 1.03), so add a past-only vol filter (trade only when |r_ROD| exceeds its 60d median or 20d vol above median) as the one pre-registered variant. title: Meta-label filter on the 5 prebuilt desk edges: of past setups like this (same trend and volatility regime), how many won? Take the trade only when that share is high
link: https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3104816 (Lopez de Prado, Advances in Financial Machine Learning 2018, ch. 3.6 meta-labeling; Joubert 2022 'Meta-Labeling: Theory and Framework', JFDS)
why: Primary model = the desk edge's own signal (desk/edges/cards: bollinger_reversion H1, donchian_trend D1, london_breakout M15, ma_cross D1, rsi2_reversion D1, on their benchmark markets EURUSD GBPUSD USDJPY AUDUSD XAUUSD US500, trades from desk.sandbox.simulate at real cost). Secondary model labels each signal 1 if its R>0, features known at the signal bar only: trend regime (sign and size of 20/60/120-bar return in ATR, price vs 200 SMA), vol regime (ATR14/ATR100, 20-bar vol tercile as in tools/range_sim.py), time of day/week for the intraday edges, distance of the stop in ATR, the edge's own last-20-trade hit rate. Start with the plain conditional frequency (win rate of past setups in the same trend x vol cell, expanding window, min 30 past trades per cell) before any GBM. HOW IT DIFFERS from the rejected meta-labels: all 8 (ml_metalabel_breakout_size AUC 0.51-0.53 book 3.34->3.32; ml_metalabel_breakout_leg dup; ml_metalabel_after_morning_fall AUC 0.465; ml_metalabel_quartet_skip corr 0.92 AUC ~0.5; ml_pooled_metalabel_intraday_legs pooled AUC 0.57-0.58 = base rate, within-leg 0.38-0.56, book 3.40->3.01-3.19; ml_regime_filter_gold_hold AUC 0.60 but skipped 73% of days, hold SR 0.53->0.15; ml_hold_gvz_regime halves 0.18/0.84; ml_cross_skip_fix_overlap AUC 0.398) filtered the book's live legs, which are already selected and tuned so their losers look like their winners. These benchmark edges are untuned textbook rules with many more trades (thousands across 6 markets) and known regime dependence (trend rules lose in chop, reversion rules lose in trends), which is where meta-labeling has signal. Kill rules fixed in advance: (1) AUC >= 0.55 WITHIN EACH EDGE out of sample (pooled AUC does not count, lesson from the pooled item); (2) beat a random-skip control that skips the same share of trades (100 draws; the filtered Sharpe must exceed the 95th percentile); (3) skip at most 50% of trades; (4) both halves (to 2017 / from 2018) improve; (5) the filtered edge passes tools/gates.py on its own and adds to the book (portfolio rule), not just beats the unfiltered edge. Walk-forward yearly with purge = the edge's max holding period and 1-bar embargo; every feature set and threshold counts as a trial (gates n_extra).
evidence: Lopez de Prado (2018) ch. 3.6: meta-labeling separates side (primary rule) from size/skip (ML), and helps most when the primary has high recall and low precision, which fits untuned breakout/MA/RSI rules. Joubert (2022) JFDS: gains come from filtering false positives of a simple primary model, measured by F1 and Sharpe against the primary alone. Our own record: 8 meta-label tries on tuned live legs failed (AUC 0.40-0.60); none were tried on the untuned benchmark edges.
result: Kill rule 1 (AUC>=0.55 within edge, walk-forward yearly from 2012): bollinger 0.549 (avg_r -0.06 after filter, still negative), donchian 0.516, ma_cross 28 OOS trades, rsi2 0.513; london_breakout 0.553 only: filtered Sharpe 0.12 all OOS (0.20 to 2017, 0.07 from 2018, below the 0.2 gate), though above random-skip p95 -0.03. Not gated: fails halves Sharpe. research/ml_metalabel_desk_benchmark_edges.py

title: Pairs trading on international equity indices (Thomakos-Wang-Schizas; Gatev distance method) as a market-neutral days leg
why: Gap: losing months (steer 2026-10-31), days horizon, off gold and off dollar pairs. Rule (Thomakos et al via Quantpedia, Gatev 2006 NBER w7032 read pages 1-12 for the method): normalise each index to 1 over a 120-day formation window, pair distance = sum of squared gaps, take the closest pairs; trade 20 days; open when the normalised spread exceeds 0.5 historical sd (Gatev uses 2 sd): long the cheap index, short the rich one, equal notional; exit on crossing or after 20 business days; one-day wait after the signal. Universe: SPXUSD, NSXUSD, GRXEUR, JPXJPY (+ any other index M1 in marketdata). With few indices run all pairs (6) with the same parameters, equal risk, not only the top 5. Suits Funded (market neutral, days). Differs from rejected Hau-Rey (equity-FX) and Baltussen reversal (single index sign): this is relative value between indices.
